# dsh-glass-theme

An Apple Liquid Glass skin for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI. Every surface in the
app is redrawn: fl

oating glass chrome over an ambient light field, an opaque
reading surface for the transcript, and o

ne material ladder shared by every
panel, popover and dialog.

Pure CSS plus a ~150-line client runtime. Nothing in the shipped app is patched;
the skin loads as a

n ordinary Harness bundle and layers its stylesheets after the
app's own.
| Light | Dark |
## What it does

- **Re-keys the app's whole token vocabulary.** The shipped theme publishes an
empty token set, so t

he palette is CSS-only. `src/css/tokens.css` re-declares
~250 `--dsw-*` custom properties on `body`

(and `body[data-ds-dark-theme]`),
which makes every page the skin has never heard of inherit the red

esign. It
also defines 11 properties the shipped build consumes but never defines.
- **Redraws every

surface** across 16 sheets: shell, sidebar, conversation,
composer, overlays, model, picker, stats,

settings, pages, workspace,
widgets, motion.
- **Replaces the composer's model picker.** `src/picke

r.js` mounts its own React
card into `conversation.input.model` and hides the host trigger: grouped

providers, a one-line description per model, the reseller price ratio as a
badge, a live peak/off-pe

ak chip that follows the SELECTED model's provider
(DeepSeek: 工作日 9:00–12:00 + 14:00–18:00, ≈2×; 智谱:

工作日 14:00–18:00,
≈2×; providers without a schedule show no chip), and an inline effort
segmented co

ntrol beside the model list (both visible at once; picking a
model keeps the card open). Configured

providers
narrow the default list; everything else stays behind one "所有供应商" row.
Selection feedback

is derived from the public directory snapshot: an
activation shows pending on the target while the h

ost-confirmed `current`
stays the only checkmark, a failed or rejected command shows a retryable
fai

lure note, and an acknowledged command that no projection confirms
within 8 seconds shows an explici

t unconfirmed note — never an automatic
rollback. The all-providers card closes only on acknowledged

oading, empty, overall error (retry via `load()`), filtered
no-match (clear the query), and partial

provider failures (a note, not a
blocker).
- **Merges the usage readouts.** `src/stats.js` replaces

the two stat pills and
the context ring with one control that opens a single panel: context pressure

and its three buckets, session timings, and the token ledger. The pill sits at

## Install
`lib/` is committed, so a clone is ready to load — installing needs no build step.

The releases page carries
the same build as a prebuilt tarball,
`dsh-glass-theme.tgz`.
Its name is v

ersion-free on purpose, so that URL keeps resolving across
releases; storefronts serve it instead of
a build-from-source command.

2. Add it to that profile's bundle list in `<profile>/package.json`:

3. Restart the Harness.

The restart is not optional: the plugin roster is composed from the profile
before the window opens,

and the host half (routes, peak-rate cache, usage
ledger) is mounted at boot. Nothing in the shippe

d app is modified — removing
the folder and the bundle entry restores the stock interface exactly.

## Build and verify
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Live probes (each needs the GUI running; they mint their own auth cookie):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`verify.mjs` is the important one. A skin is nothing but selectors, so a wrong
hash prefix or a rena

med local is a silently dead rule — no error, no warning,
just a surface that keeps its old look. Th

e tool resolves every token against
`research/shipped-class-map.json` (extracted from the installed

app) and fails
the build on a miss.

`style-lifecycle-check.mjs` guards the other half of the mount contract: the
reconcile must be bound

ed. It runs the built bundle in a stub DOM whose mutation
records deliver asynchronously and counts

actual stylesheet DOM writes, so a
mount that keeps moving its own tags and reacting to the records

of those moves
cannot pass as "idempotent". Host batches, partial and total sheet removal,
`<head>`

replacement, missing `MutationObserver`/`requestAnimationFrame`,
disposal with a repair still queued

, and a superseding mount are all covered;
the original defective implementation is preserved inside

the tool as scenario 1
and must keep failing to converge, so the defect stays reproducible.
### The inventories `verify.mjs` resolves against

The app generates its CSS-module class names (`_local_hash`), so the only honest
way to check a sele

ctor is against the classes the *installed* build emits. Those
maps are generated, not committed — t

hey contain the app's own stylesheet text,
which is not ours to redistribute. One step each:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Both write into `../research/` — one level above the package, so an installed
copy never carries the

m. `extract-inventories.mjs` auto-detects a local install
when `--asar` is omitted.

`assert-built.mjs` exists because the bundle escapes its own CSS: each sheet is
embedded as a JSON s

tring, so a newline is the two characters `\` `n`. A regex
written against the source file misses in

the bundle for that reason alone —
which looks exactly like a lost rule. The tool unescapes once an

d then asserts
both the rules that must exist and the ones that must not.
## Keyboard navigation and layer coordination
All skin-owned popovers, dialogs, drawers, and menus register with a unified coordinator (`src/layer
s.js`). One coordinator instance is scoped to the client session and shared by all skin component fa
One coordinator instance is scoped to the client session and shared by all skin component factories:
- **Top-layer Escape and outside routing**: Only the topmost open layer handles an Escape keypress o
r outside click. Closing a child card (e.g. the picker's all-providers card) leaves the parent layer

. Closing a child card (e.g. the picker's all-providers card) leaves the parent layer open.
